newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Rebels say PNG's Panguna mine to stay closed.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Rebels say PNG's Panguna mine to stay closed.

text.p: Bougainville rebels would not allow Papua New Guinea's giant Panguna copper mine, owned by Bougainville Copper Ltd, to reopen until a political solution had been reached in their secessionist conflict, a rebel spokesman said on Monday.

Papua New Guinea Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan has said his government wants to buy RTZ-CRA's 53.6 percent stake in the giant Panguna copper mine as part of a solution to the secessionist crisis on Bougainville.

"What he (Chan) is suggsting is not going to change our position," said Moses Havini, Sydney-based spokesman for the Bougainville Interim Government, which represents the Bougainville Revolutionary Army (BRA).
"We closed the CRA mine in 1989 and it will remain so until a political agenda for the people of Bougainville is settled," Havini said.
CRA has estimated it would cost more than 450 million kina (US$328 million) to restart the mine.
Chan has said the purchase of the mine would enable Papua New Guinea to restructure ownership, financing and operational aspects of the mine, leading to compensation for landowners.
Landowners disgruntled over royalty payments from the mine in central Bougainville sabotaged the mine in the late 1980s, with their wave of violence becoming a secessionist revolt.
Havini rejected Chan's suggestion that by buying-back the mine Bougainvilleans could benefit financially.
"Chan probably suffers from memory lapses. We have unsucessfully tried to negotiate with the PNG government...for the last 25 years now," Havini told a news conference.
"Right throughout this period not once did the PNG government and CRA come to the negotiating table with us."
Bougainville Copper Ltd operated the giant Panguna mine on the island for 17 years until a secessionist rebellion led to its closure in 1989.

CRA, the Australian part of Anglo-Australia dual listed mining giant RTZ-CRA, said earlier it had not held any discussions with the PNG government about the Bougainville stake but that it expected it would shortly receive a formal approach from the government.
The PNG government owns 19.1 percent of Bougainville Copper.
Bougainville shares were four cents higher at 60 cents on Monday at 2.00 p.m. (0300 GMT). -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
